title: Kestrel Runner — launch spot
storyboard:
# Kestrel Runner — launch spot

Length 12 seconds at 30 fps. Deliver three cuts: 16:9 (1920x1080), 9:16 (1080x1920), 1:1 (1080x1080).

## Shot 1 (0:00–0:03) Product hero
- A teal running shoe with an orange sole slides in from the left over a dark night-city background.
- The shoe is fully inside the frame by 0:01.
- Caption reads exactly: Run the city
- The caption is fully visible by 0:01.

## Shot 2 (0:03–0:07) Detail
- Close-up of the orange sole, same teal and orange colourway as shot 1.
- The KESTREL wordmark is absent at 0:03 and fully visible by 0:05.
- A price tag reads exactly: €149 and is visible at 0:04 and at 0:06.

## Shot 3 (0:07–0:12) Call to action
- Headline reads exactly: Out 28 November
- A button labelled exactly: Get early access, fully visible by 0:09.
- The KESTREL wordmark is visible throughout shot 3.

## Delivery rules
- On the 9:16 cut, no text or button sits in the bottom 35% or the top 14% of the frame.
- On the 9:16 cut, every piece of text is set at 48px or larger so it reads on a phone.
- On every cut, all text stays fully inside the frame.

versions.summary:
I've written `src/Video.tsx` in one pass. I haven't rendered it or run Kane on it yet, so the timings and safe-zone positions below are worked out on paper, not tested.

**Timeline:** 360 frames at 30 fps, split into three shots: frames 0–90, 90–210 and 210–360. Each shot is its own `<Sequence>`, and `composition.shots` lists the same three.

**Shot 1 – Product hero**
- The teal shoe with its orange sole is drawn entirely in SVG. It slides in from the left over a night-city background and is fully in frame by frame 22, ahead of the 0:01 mark.
- The city has three layers of buildings with lit windows, blinking roof beacons, a moon glow and car light trails on the street.
- Speed streaks appear while the shoe is moving, then it bobs gently and the camera pushes in slowly.
- "Run the city" is fully visible by frame 24.

**Shot 2 – Detail**
- A close-up of the same shoe, panning slowly along the orange sole with a highlight sweeping across it.
- KESTREL is invisible at 0:03 and fully visible by 0:04.5.
- An orange price tag reading "€149" pops in at about 0:03.1 and stays until the cut, so it's on screen at 0:04 and at 0:06.

**Shot 3 – Call to action**
- KESTREL is fully visible from

"Run the city" is now a big, bold lower-third subtitle on 16:9 and 1:1. On 9:16 I couldn't put it near the bottom, because `storyboard.md` bans text in the bottom 35% of that cut. I placed it as low as that allows instead. I haven't rendered it yet, so Kane's check when this turn ends will be the first real test.

**What changed (Shot 1 only):**
- **Style:** heavy 900-weight white text on a dark, slightly see-through rounded panel, like social-video captions. A teal-to-orange line wipes along the panel's bottom edge as an accent.
- **Placement:**
  - 16:9 (120px) and 1:1 (100px): the panel's bottom edge sits 7% above the bottom of the frame.
  - 9:16 (110px): the panel's bottom edge is at 62% of the frame height (about y = 1190 of 1920). That's the lowest it can go while staying above the 65% line, which is at y = 1248.
- **Animation:** the panel rises and fades in over frames 2–16, then the text slides up inside it. The caption is fully visible by frame 24, still before the 0:01 deadline.
- **No overlap:** by my layout maths, the shoe ends above the caption on every cut, so none of the shoe positions needed changing.

To push the 9:16 caption further down, the 35% rule in the stor

"Get early access" is now a huge full-width install bar. It's pinned to the bottom on 16:9 and 1:1. On 9:16 it can't go there, because `storyboard.md` bans text and buttons in the bottom 35% of that cut, so it sits right on that limit instead. I haven't rendered this, so Kane's check when the turn ends will be the first real test.

**The bar (Shot 3, every cut):**
- **Size:** it runs the full width of the frame with a small 4–5% inset on each side. The text is 900-weight: 76px on 16:9, 72px on 9:16 and 64px on 1:1.
- **Look:** a bold orange gradient with a highlight along its top edge and a darker bottom edge for depth. The highlight sweep and the pulsing orange glow are kept.
- **Placement:**
  - 16:9 and 1:1: the bar's bottom edge sits 5% above the bottom of the frame, over a dark gradient so it reads like a docked app bar.
  - 9:16: the bar's bottom edge is at 63% of the frame height (about y = 1210), just above the 65% limit at y = 1248.
- **Animation:** the bar fades in and opens outward from the centre while rising 24px. It's fully visible by frame 46 of the shot, about 0:08.5, ahead of the 0:09 requirement.
- **No overlap:** by my layout maths, nothing collides with the bar

Almost all type is now 900 weight and 60% bigger, but two things didn't land fully. The "Get early access" button text on 9:16 and 1:1 only grew by about 1.35×, and 9:16 text still stays out of the bottom 35%. I haven't rendered this, so the widths are my estimates for the system font. Kane's check when the turn ends will be the first real test of whether everything fits.

| Text | 16:9 | 9:16 | 1:1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| "Run the city" caption | 192 | 176 | 160 |
| KESTREL (shot 2) | 240 | 189 | 166 |
| €149 price tag | 154 | 160 | 128 |
| KESTREL (shot 3) | 109 | 128 | 96 |
| "Out 28 November" | 240 | 160 | 134 |
| "Get early access" button | 122 | ≈97 (target 115) | ≈97 (target 102) |

**What I changed to make it fit:**
- **Button:** on the 1080-wide cuts, "Get early access" can't fit on one line at full 1.6×, so the size is capped to what fits the bar. If my width estimate is off, the text wraps to two lines rather than spilling out of the frame.
- **Stacking instead of shrinking:** the caption and the headline go to two lines wherever one line won't fit. That gives "Run the" / "city" and "Out 28" / "November", and the size stays at the full 1.6×.
- **Tighter wordmark:** KESTREL

usecases.title: Deliver the Kestrel Runner launch spot in three cuts
Inspect storyboard cuts in a browser contact sheet

criteria.text: The 9:16 cut measures 1080×1920 pixels.
The 16:9 cut measures 1920×1080 pixels.
The 1:1 cut measures 1080×1080 pixels.
Each cut is 12 seconds long.
Each cut runs at 30 frames per second.
Shot 1 occupies 0:00–0:03 on each cut.
Shot 2 occupies 0:03–0:07 on each cut.
Shot 3 occupies 0:07–0:12 on each cut.

expected.operand: teal running shoe with orange sole sliding in from the left during shot 1

criteria.text: Shot 1 shows a teal running shoe with an orange sole sliding in from the left.
Shot 1 has a dark night-city background.
The shoe is fully inside the frame by 0:01 on each cut.
The shot 1 caption reads exactly 'Run the city' on each cut.
The shot 1 caption is fully visible by 0:01 on each cut.

expected.operand: close-up orange sole in shot 2 matching shot 1 teal-and-orange colourway

criteria.text: Shot 2 shows a close-up of the orange sole in the same teal-and-orange colourway as shot 1.

expected.operand: visible KESTREL wordmark in shot 2 at 0:03

criteria.text: The KESTREL wordmark is absent at 0:03 in shot 2 on each cut.

expected.operand: fully visible KESTREL wordmark in shot 2 at 0:05

criteria.text: The KESTREL wordmark is fully visible by 0:05 in shot 2 on each cut.
The shot 2 price tag reads exactly '€149' on each cut.
The price tag is visible at 0:04 on each cut.
The price tag is visible at 0:06 on each cut.
The shot 3 headline reads exactly 'Out 28 November' on each cut.
The shot 3 button is labelled exactly 'Get early access' on each cut.

expected.operand: fully visible Get early access button at 0:09

criteria.text: The shot 3 early-access button is fully visible by 0:09 on each cut.

expected.operand: KESTREL wordmark visible in every shot 3 frame

criteria.text: The KESTREL wordmark is visible throughout shot 3 on each cut.

expected.operand: text or button overlapping top 14% of 9:16 frame

criteria.text: No text or button on the 9:16 cut occupies the top 14% of the frame.

expected.operand: text or button overlapping bottom 35% of 9:16 frame

criteria.text: No text or button on the 9:16 cut occupies the bottom 35% of the frame.
Every piece of text on the 9:16 cut has a rendered size of at least 48px.

expected.operand: every visible text layer fully inside its cut's frame

criteria.text: All text stays fully inside the frame on every cut.

tests.title: Check every portrait text layer's rendered size
tests.summary: Inspect every piece of text in portrait frames for rendered size >=48px.

steps.heading: Step 1
steps.body: Open {{sheet_url}}?cut=9x16 in the browser and wait until the Kestrel Runner contact sheet says ready; inspect each displayed text layer's computed rendered font size alongside its frame-containment facts, then assert every displayed text layer renders at 48px or larger and is fully inside the frame.

tests.title: Check portrait reserved bands across the contact sheet
tests.summary: Inspect all portrait text and buttons against the top 14% and bottom 35% bands across the sheet.

steps.heading: Step 1
steps.body: Open {{sheet_url}}?cut=9x16 in the browser and wait until the Kestrel Runner contact sheet says ready; turn on Show safe zones and inspect every displayed text and button layer against the top 14% and bottom 35% of the 1080×1920 frame and the text-layer in-frame facts, then assert no displayed text or button occupies either reserved band and every displayed text layer is fully inside the frame.

tests.title: Inspect landscape launch cut and timed content
tests.summary: Inspect the 16:9 cut's dimensions, duration, frame rate, shot intervals, timed product and text appearances and all-text containment.

steps.heading: Step 1
steps.body: Open {{sheet_url}}?cut=16x9 in the browser and wait until the Kestrel Runner contact-sheet header says ready; inspect its measured metadata and listed shots, then assert the cut measures 1920×1080 pixels, lasts 12 seconds at 30 fps, and lists shot intervals 0:00–0:03, 0:03–0:07 and 0:07–0:12.

steps.heading: Step 2
steps.body: On the 16:9 sheet, inspect the displayed shot-1 frames and layer facts through 0:01, then assert the teal shoe with orange sole slides from the left over a dark night-city background, the shoe is fully inside the frame by 0:01, and the fully visible caption at 0:01 reads exactly 'Run the city'.

steps.heading: Step 3
steps.body: On the 16:9 sheet, inspect shot 2 and its facts at 0:04, 0:05 and 0:06, then assert the orange-sole close-up matches the shot-1 teal-and-orange colourway, the KESTREL wordmark is fully visible by 0:05, and the price tag reads exactly '€149' and is visible at both 0:04 and 0:06.

steps.heading: Step 4
steps.body: On the 16:9 sheet, inspect shot-3 frames and layer facts including 0:09, then assert the headline reads exactly 'Out 28 November' and the button label reads exactly 'Get early access' and is fully visible by 0:09.

steps.heading: Step 5
steps.body: On the 16:9 sheet, inspect the frame-containment fact for every displayed text layer in every displayed frame, then assert every displayed text layer is fully inside the frame.
